english.title: Attempted buggery - person over 16 years with girl under 16 years
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being of or over the age of 16 years, attempted to commit buggery with a girl under the age of 16 years, **(..SPECIFY NAME..), who was aged **(..SPECIFY AGE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12(1) of, and Schedule 2 to, the Sexual Offences Act 1956 and section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
person aged 16 years or over
attempted to
commit sexual intercourse per anus
with girl under 16 years of age

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence may also be committed against a boy, see H7994.
(ii) If offence committed without the person's consent on or after 3.11.94 then charge rape.
(iii) This offence is included in Schedule 1 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997, therefore a person convicted or cautioned for this offence must comply with the requirements of section 2 of that Act.
(iv) This offence is included in Schedule 2 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997, therefore a person committing this offence outside the United Kingdom may in certain circumstances be prosecuted for that offence in England, Wales or Northern Ireland.
(v) The age of consent was lowered to sixteen years on 8.1.01 by the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 2000.
(vi) Repealed by s.140 of, and Schedule 7 to, the Sexual Offences Act 2003.
(vii) This offence is now obsolete with no exact modern equivalent. Historical records must be reviewed case-by-case and graded/retained under MoPI according to the modern equivalent, taking into account individual case circumstances, victim capacity and consent, and ages of victim and offender.

other.penalty:
Indictment: maximum life imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
